ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a closed single-loop series circuit, with power supply E on the left side, ordinary diode VD and LED connected in series in sequence above, and resistor R connected in series at the bottom. All components are in the same loop, so the current is the same. Reasoning: It is known that the electromotive force of the power supply E = 6 V, the forward voltage drop of the silicon diode is 0.7 V, the forward voltage drop of the white LED is 3.3 V, and resistor R = 10 Ω. According to Kirchhoff's voltage law, the power supply voltage equals the sum of the voltage drops across the two diodes and the voltage drop across the resistor, so the voltage across the resistor is 6 - 0.7 - 3.3 = 2.0 V. By Ohm's law I = V_R / R = 2.0 / 10 = 0.2 A. Since it is a series circuit, the LED current is also 0.2 A.
